title: Tests build a new git repo for every case
what: Build a test repository once per test class (or once per run) and give each case a copy of it (a folder copy takes a few ms against about 160 ms for git init plus commits), as git's own test suite and pytest's class-scoped fixtures do. Start with the files that start the most git: test_guard_test_name (one test starts 1524 git in 91 s), test_queue (7228 git in 97 tests, 6766 from the test process itself), test_gate (1937).
why: Measured 29 Oct by the gate-speed design: one run of the 1753 library tests starts 61,379 git processes, about 35 per test; inside these tests one git call costs 60-67 ms of wall at load 20. Owner, 29 Oct, verbatim: "А почему вообще так много вызовов git ?". IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen).
failing_case: 29 Oct, master ee932b26: tests/test_guard_test_name.py, one test starts 1524 git processes and takes 91 s.
pass_cases: The same tests pass with a template repository built once per class and a private copy of it made for each test (a file copy, no git calls), so a test that writes never shares a repository with another; their git starts and wall time are measured before and after.

said: Тесты создают репозиторий один раз на группу тестов, а не на каждый тест - но это поможет только если команды читают, если они пишут то мы получим конфликты, разве нет ?

fact: Edited pass_cases: 29 Oct, owner: a shared repository only helps tests that read; tests that write would collide. Measured by the front the same day at load 30: building a 5-commit template takes 252 ms (18 git calls); a plain file copy of it 18 ms per test, an APFS clone (cp -c) 27 ms; a commit in a copy works and leaves the template untouched.
